title: B300 cost calibration required a broker job-id environment variable that the broker does not inject

evidence.events: events.jsonl lines 30-32: broker_started assigned gpuq-d5577450f13a to physical GPU 2; correctness then ended with infra_error
evidence.stage: stages/correctness/stderr.log reports 'container calibration requires one broker-assigned GPU'; receipt.json records broker execution, exit 1, and physical GPU 2
evidence.source_boundary: The broker child environment contains CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES but does not declare GPUQ_JOB_ID (agent-gpu-broker/src/agent_gpu_broker/broker.py::Broker._execute).

observation: The local compile stage passed and retained 12 CUBINs and 24 CPU oracle files. After the broker assigned physical GPU 2, the host container wrapper rejected an absent GPUQ_JOB_ID before launching Docker. The run produced no device correctness, CUPTI timing, empirical model or GPU-savings evidence. The broker job ended; no task container or queued resubmission remained.
proposed_change: Read the exact broker job id from the GPU Infra daemon's running stage state after broker_started, requiring the same run id, stage id and single physical GPU as the broker-provided CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Pass that identity to the pinned container and require the final stage receipt to match. Retain fail-closed refusal on any mismatch; keep the frozen v3 run unchanged.

verified_by.observed: The successor resolved the original event at events.jsonl line 30 to gpuq-d5577450f13a on GPU 2. Replaying the same observation with the wrong stage or GPU was refused.
verified_by.contracts: 38 relevant documentation and empirical-cost contract tests passed at 627d63bc in an isolated worktree.
verified_by.limits: This closes the software broker-identity failure only. A new frozen B300 campaign is required to verify device correctness, timing quality, model calibration and any saved GPU searches.
